units.zh: 馮道，字可道，瀛州景城人。
units.en: Feng Dao, styled Kedao, came from Jingcheng in Yingzhou.
units.literal: Feng Dao, courtesy name Kedao, was a native of Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.

units.zh: 其先為農為儒，不恒其業。
units.en: His forebears had farmed and studied by turns, never keeping to one calling.
units.literal: His ancestors had been farmers and scholars by turns, without a fixed occupation.

units.zh: 道少純厚，好學能文，不恥惡衣食，負米奉親之外，惟以披誦吟諷為事，雖大雪擁戶，凝塵滿席，湛如也。
units.en: As a young man Feng Dao was guileless and steady, loved learning and wrote well, and was unashamed of coarse food and clothes. Beyond carrying grain home for his parents, he did nothing but read and chant; even when snow piled against his door and dust caked his mat, he remained wholly at ease.
units.literal: In youth Dao was plain and sincere, fond of study and skilled in letters, and not ashamed of poor food and clothing; apart from carrying rice to support his parents, he devoted himself solely to reading aloud and reciting poetry. Even when heavy snow blocked the doorway and dust lay thick on his mat, he remained serene.

units.zh: 天祐中，劉守光署為幽州掾。
units.en: In the Tianyou period Liu Shouguang made him a staff officer in Youzhou.
units.literal: During the Tianyou era Liu Shouguang appointed him an aide in You Prefecture.

units.zh: 守光引兵伐中山，訪於僚屬，道常以利害箴之，守光怒，置於獄中，尋為人所救免。
units.en: When Shouguang marched on Zhongshan and asked his staff for counsel, Dao repeatedly warned him of the risks. Shouguang flew into a rage and threw him in prison, but others soon secured his release.
units.literal: When Shouguang led troops to attack Zhongshan and consulted his staff, Dao often admonished him on advantage and harm. Shouguang grew angry and had him imprisoned, but he was soon rescued and released by others.

units.zh: 守光敗，遁歸太原，監軍使張承業辟為本院巡官。
units.en: After Shouguang's defeat Dao fled to Taiyuan, where the army supervisory commissioner Zhang Chengye took him on as a headquarters inspector.
units.literal: When Shouguang was defeated, Dao fled back to Taiyuan, and the army supervisory commissioner Zhang Chengye recruited him as an inspector of the headquarters.

units.zh: 承業重其文章履行，甚見待遇。
units.en: Chengye prized his writing and character and treated him with marked favor.
units.literal: Chengye valued his literary talent and conduct and treated him with great favor.

units.zh: 時有周元豹者，善人倫鑒，與道不洽，謂承業曰：「馮生無前程，公不可過用。」
units.en: There was a Zhou Yuanbao at the time, skilled at reading men, who disliked Dao. He told Chengye, "Feng has no great career ahead—do not promote him too far."
units.literal: At the time there was a Zhou Yuanbao, skilled in judging character, who was on poor terms with Dao. He told Chengye, "Master Feng has no future ahead of him; you, sir, must not employ him too highly.

units.zh: 時河東記室盧質聞之曰：「我曾見杜黃裳司空寫真圖，道之狀貌酷類焉，將來必副大用，元豹之言不足信也。」
units.en: Lu Zhi, recorder of the Hedong commandery, heard this and said, "I once saw the portrait of Du Huangshang, Minister of Works—Feng Dao looks remarkably like him. He is bound for high office; Yuanbao's judgment cannot be trusted."
units.literal: When Lu Zhi, recorder of Hedong, heard this he said, "I once saw the portrait of Minister of Works Du Huangshang; Dao's appearance closely resembles it. He will surely prove fit for great employment in the future—Yuanbao's words are not to be trusted."

units.zh: 承業尋薦為霸府從事，俄署太原掌書記，時莊宗並有河北，文翰甚繁，一以委之。
units.en: Chengye soon recommended him as staff in the hegemon's headquarters and shortly named him chief secretary at Taiyuan. Zhuangzong had just taken Hebei, and the flood of documents was left entirely to Dao.
units.literal: Chengye soon recommended him as an aide in the hegemon's headquarters, and shortly thereafter appointed him chief secretary at Taiyuan. At that time Emperor Zhuangzong had united Hebei, and official correspondence was extremely heavy—all of it was entrusted to Dao.

units.zh: 莊宗與梁軍夾河對壘，一日，郭崇韜以諸校伴食數多，主者不辦，請少罷減。
units.en: Zhuangzong and the Liang forces were camped on opposite banks of the Yellow River. One day Guo Chongtao, finding that too many officers shared the commander's table for the staff to supply, asked that the number be cut back.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong and the Liang army faced each other across the Yellow River. One day Guo Chongtao, noting that the number of officers dining with the commander was too large for the commissary to manage, asked that it be reduced somewhat.

units.zh: 莊宗怒曰：「孤為效命者設食都不自由，其河北三鎮，令三軍別擇一人為帥，孤請歸太原以避賢路。」
units.en: Zhuangzong burst out, "I cannot even decide who eats at my table for men who die in my service! Let each of the three Hebei armies pick its own commander—I will go back to Taiyuan and make way for better men."
units.literal: Zhuangzong said angrily, "I cannot even freely set out food for those who risk their lives for me! Let the three circuits of Hebei have each army choose its own commander; I shall return to Taiyuan to yield the path to worthier men.

units.zh: 遽命道對面草詞，將示其眾。
units.en: He at once ordered Dao to draft an edict on the spot to read before the army.
units.literal: He immediately ordered Dao to draft an edict face to face, intending to show it to the troops.

units.zh: 道執筆久之，莊宗正色促焉，道徐起對曰：「道所掌筆硯，敢不供職。
units.en: Dao held his brush a long time while Zhuangzong glared and urged him on. Dao rose slowly and said, "The brush is mine to serve you with—how could I refuse my duty?
units.literal: Dao held his brush a long while. Zhuangzong, with a stern face, pressed him. Dao rose slowly and replied, "The brush and ink I hold are at Your Majesty's service—how would I dare not perform my duty?

units.zh: 今大王屢集大功，方平南寇，崇韜所諫，未至過當，阻拒之則可，不可以向來之言，喧動群議，敵人若知，謂大王君臣之不和矣。
units.en: Your Highness has won victory after victory and is about to crush the southern foe. Chongtao's counsel was not excessive—you may turn it down, but do not let your earlier words stir the whole camp. If the enemy hears of it, they will think ruler and minister are divided.
units.literal: Now Your Highness has repeatedly achieved great merit and is on the verge of pacifying the southern enemy. Chongtao's advice has not gone beyond what is proper; you may refuse it, but you must not let your earlier words stir up widespread debate. If the enemy learns of it, they will say that lord and minister are at odds.

units.zh: 幸熟而思之，則天下幸甚也。」
units.en: If you weigh this carefully, the realm will be greatly fortunate."
units.literal: If you will reflect on this carefully, it will be a great fortune for the realm.

units.zh: 俄而崇韜入謝，因道為之解焉，人始重其膽量。
units.en: Soon Chongtao came in to apologize, and Dao smoothed things over for him; from then on men respected his nerve.
units.literal: Shortly afterward Chongtao came in to apologize, and Dao interceded for him; people then began to respect his courage.

units.zh: 莊宗即位鄴宮，除省郎，充翰林學士，自綠衣賜紫。
units.en: When Zhuangzong was enthroned at Ye, Dao was made a Secretariat secretary and Hanlin academician, promoted from green to purple robes.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at the Ye palace, Dao was made a secretary in the Secretariat and appointed Hanlin Academician, advancing from green robes to purple.

units.zh: 梁平，遷中書舍人、戶部侍郎。
units.en: After the Liang were subdued he was promoted to Secretariat drafting secretary and Vice Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: When the Liang were pacified, he was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 丁父憂，持服於景城。
units.en: When his father died he went into mourning at Jingcheng.
units.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning at Jingcheng.

units.zh: 〈（《談苑》：道聞父喪，即徒步見星以行，家人從後持衣囊追及之。）〉
units.en: (Conversational Garden: When he heard of his father's death, Dao set out on foot by starlight while his family hurried after with a bag of clothes and overtook him.)
units.literal: (Tan Yuan, Conversational Garden: On hearing of his father's death, Dao set out on foot by starlight. His family followed behind with a bag of clothes and caught up with him.)

units.zh: 遇歲儉，所得俸余悉賑於鄉里，道之所居惟蓬茨而已，凡牧宰饋遺，鬥粟匹帛無所受焉。
units.en: In a famine year he gave away every spare coin of his salary to the neighborhood. He lived in nothing but a thatched hut, and refused every gift from magistrates, whether grain by the peck or cloth by the bolt.
units.literal: When the year was lean, he distributed all his remaining salary to the countryside. Dao's dwelling was only a thatched hut. Whatever local officials sent as gifts—a peck of grain or a bolt of cloth—he never accepted.

units.zh: 時契丹方盛，素聞道名，欲掠而取之，會邊人有備，獲免。
units.en: The Khitan were then at their height and had long heard of Dao; they meant to carry him off by force, but the border people were ready, and he was spared.
units.literal: At that time the Khitan were growing powerful and had long heard of Dao's reputation; they wished to seize him by force, but because the border people were on guard, he escaped harm.

units.zh: 明宗入洛，遽謂近臣安重誨曰：「先帝時馮道郎中何在？」
units.en: When Mingzong entered Luoyang he suddenly asked his confidant An Chonghui, "Where is Feng Dao, who served as director under the late emperor?"
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong entered Luoyang, he abruptly asked his close adviser An Chonghui, "Where is Director Feng Dao from the former emperor's reign?

units.zh: 重誨曰：「近除翰林學士。」
units.en: Chonghui replied, "He was recently made Hanlin academician."
units.literal: Chonghui said, "He was recently appointed Hanlin Academician."

units.zh: 明宗曰：「此人朕素諳委，甚好宰相。」
units.en: Mingzong said, "I have known and trusted him for years—he would make an excellent chief counselor."
units.literal: Mingzong said, "I have long known and trusted this man—he would make an excellent chief counselor."

units.zh: 俄拜端明殿學士，端明之號，自道始也。
units.en: He was soon made academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity—the title itself began with Dao.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity; the title "Illuminated Clarity" began with Dao.

units.zh: 未幾，遷中書侍郎、刑部尚書、平章事。
units.en: Before long he rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Justice, and Grand Councilor.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Justice, and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 凡孤寒士子，抱才業、素知識者皆與引用；
units.en: He advanced every poor scholar of talent he had long known;
units.literal: All poor scholars of talent whom he had long known he brought into office;

units.zh: 唐末衣冠，履行浮躁者必抑而鎮之。
units.en: while he checked and humbled late-Tang officials whose conduct was frivolous.
units.literal: as for late-Tang officials whose conduct was frivolous, he always restrained and subdued them.

units.zh: 有工部侍郎任贊，因班退，與同列戲道於後曰：「若急行，必遺下《兔園冊》。」
units.en: Ren Zan, Vice Minister of Works, jested behind Dao as the court filed out: "Walk fast and he'll drop his Rabbit Garden Primer."
units.literal: There was Ren Zan, Vice Minister of Works, who as the court was dismissing jested behind Dao to his colleagues, "If he walks fast, he is sure to drop his Rabbit Garden Primer.

units.zh: 道知之，召贊謂曰：「《兔園冊》皆名儒所集，道能諷之，中朝士子止看文場秀句，便為舉業，皆竊取公聊，何淺狹之甚耶！」
units.en: Dao heard of it and summoned Zan. "The Rabbit Garden Primer was compiled by eminent scholars, and I can recite it. Yet today's court literati skim flashy examination couplets and call that a career—they merely crib from grand ministers. How petty!"
units.literal: Dao learned of it and summoned Zan, saying, "The Rabbit Garden Primer was compiled by eminent Confucians, and I can recite it. Yet court scholars today read only clever lines from the examination field and call that their preparation for office—they all plagiarize from high ministers. How shallow and narrow!"

units.zh: 贊大愧焉。
units.en: Zan was thoroughly shamed.
units.literal: Zan was deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：《兔園策》者，鄉校俚儒教田夫牧子之所誦也。
units.en: (Ouyang Xiu's History says the Rabbit Garden Stratagems was what rustic village teachers had farm boys and herdsmen memorize.)
units.literal: (Ouyang's History says: The Rabbit Garden Stratagems is what village-school rustic teachers have farmers' sons and herdsboys recite.)

units.zh: 《北夢瑣言》云：《兔園策》乃徐、庾文體，非鄙樸之談，但家藏一本，人多賤之。
units.en: Idle Talk of Northern Dreams says it was written in the manner of Xu Ling and Yu Xin, not in crude village prose—but because every home had a copy, people despised it.
units.literal: Idle Talk of Northern Dreams says: The Rabbit Garden Stratagems is in the style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin—not vulgar speech—but because every household keeps a copy, many look down on it.

units.zh: 《困學紀聞》云：《兔園策府》三十卷，唐蔣王惲令僚佐杜嗣先仿應科目策，自設問對，引經史為訓註。
units.en: Notes from Studying amid Difficulty says the Rabbit Garden Stratagem Treasury ran to thirty scrolls: in Tang, Prince Jiang Yun had his aide Du Sizian imitate civil-service policy questions, compose his own Q&A, and annotate them from the classics and histories.
units.literal: Notes from Studying amid Difficulty says: The Rabbit Garden Stratagem Treasury runs to thirty scrolls. In Tang, Prince Jiang Yun ordered his aide Du Sizian to model it on examination policy questions, setting questions and answers himself and citing the classics and histories for commentary.

units.zh: 惲，太宗子，故用梁王兔園名其書，馮道《兔園策》謂此也。）〉
units.en: Yun was a son of Taizong, so the book took the Rabbit Garden of the Prince of Liang as its title—this is the work Feng Dao meant by the Rabbit Garden Stratagems.)〉
units.literal: Yun was a son of Emperor Taizong, hence the book was named for the Rabbit Garden of the Prince of Liang—this is what Feng Dao's Rabbit Garden Stratagems refers to.)〉

units.zh: 復有梁朝宰臣李琪，每以文章自擅，曾進《賀平中山王都表》云：「復真定之逆賊」。
units.en: Li Qi, a Liang chief minister, also prided himself on his prose. He once submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Wang Du of Zhongshan that read, "The rebel of Zhending is recovered."
units.literal: There was also Li Qi, a chief minister of the Liang, who always prided himself on his literary skill. He once submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Wang Du of Zhongshan, saying, "We have recovered the rebel of Zhending."

units.zh: 道讓琪曰：「昨來收復定州，非真定也。」
units.en: Dao corrected him: "What was recovered was Dingzhou, not Zhending."
units.literal: Dao reproved Qi, saying, "The place recovered yesterday was Ding Prefecture, not Zhending.

units.zh: 琪昧於地理，頓至折角。
units.en: Qi knew nothing of geography and was utterly humiliated.
units.literal: Qi was ignorant of geography and was instantly put to shame.

units.zh: 其後百僚上明宗徽號凡三章，道自為之，其文渾然，非流俗之體，舉朝服焉。
units.en: Later, when the bureaucracy submitted three drafts of honorific titles for Mingzong, Dao wrote them himself in a rounded, elevated style far from common hackwork, and the whole court admired them.
units.literal: Later, when the hundred officials presented three chapters proposing honorific titles for Mingzong, Dao wrote them himself. The prose was rounded and full, not in the vulgar style, and the whole court admired it.

units.zh: 道尤長於篇詠，秉筆則成，典麗之外，義含古道，必為遠近傳寫，故漸畏其高深，由是班行肅然，無澆漓之態。
units.en: Dao excelled above all at poetry: he took up the brush and the piece was finished—elegant yet steeped in the old Way, and always copied far and wide. Men gradually stood in awe of his depth, and the court ranks grew grave, without frivolity.
units.literal: Dao was especially skilled at verse; he took up the brush and the work was done. Beyond elegance and beauty, his meaning held the ancient Way, and his pieces were always copied near and far. Gradually people came to stand in awe of his depth, and the court ranks grew solemn, without frivolous airs.

units.zh: 繼改門下侍郎、戶部吏部尚書、集賢殿弘文館大學士，加尚書左僕射，封始平郡公。
units.en: He was then made Vice Director of the Chancellery, Minister of Revenue and Personnel, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Hongwen Institute, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Shiping.
units.literal: He was then made Vice Director of the Chancellery, Minister of Revenue and of Personnel, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Hongwen Institute, promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Shiping Commandery.

units.zh: 一日，道因上謁既退，明宗顧謂侍臣曰：「馮道性純儉，頃在德勝寨居一茅庵，與從人同器食，臥則芻槁一束，其心晏如也。
units.en: One day, after Dao had paid his respects and left, Mingzong told his attendants, "Feng Dao is plain and frugal by nature. At Desheng Stockade he lived in a hut, ate from the same bowl as his men, and slept on a bundle of straw—yet his mind was wholly at peace.
units.literal: One day, after Dao had paid his respects and withdrawn, Mingzong turned to his attendants and said, "Feng Dao is by nature plain and frugal. Not long ago at Desheng Stockade he lived in a thatched hut, ate from the same bowl as his followers, and slept on a single bundle of straw—yet his mind was perfectly at ease.

units.zh: 及以父憂退歸鄉里，自耕樵采，與農夫雜處，略不以素貴介懷，真士大夫也。」
units.en: When he went home for his father's mourning he farmed and cut wood himself, lived among peasants, and never let his former status show—a true gentleman."
units.literal: When he withdrew to his home district in mourning for his father, he plowed, cut firewood, and gathered fuel himself, mingling with farmers without the least air of former rank—a true gentleman.

units.zh: 天成、長興中，天下屢稔，朝廷無事。
units.en: Through the Tiancheng and Changxing reigns harvests followed harvests and the court knew no trouble.
units.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing the realm enjoyed repeated harvests and the court was untroubled.

units.zh: 明宗每禦延英，留道訪以外事，道曰：「陛下以至德承天，天以有年表瑞，更在日慎一日，以答天心。
units.en: Whenever Mingzong held court at Yanying he kept Dao to discuss affairs of state. Dao said, "Your Majesty rules by supreme virtue; Heaven answers with good harvests. You must be more careful with each passing day to answer Heaven.
units.literal: Whenever Mingzong held court at Yanying Hall he kept Dao behind to consult on outside affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty, with supreme virtue, receives Heaven's mandate; Heaven shows its favor in years of plenty. You must be more careful day by day to answer Heaven's heart.

units.zh: 臣每記在先皇霸府日，曾奉使中山，徑井陘之險，憂馬有蹶失，不敢怠於銜轡；
units.en: I remember when I served the late emperor's headquarters I was sent to Zhongshan and took the perilous Jingxing Pass. Fearing my horse might fall, I never slackened the reins;
units.literal: I recall that in the days of the former emperor's hegemon's headquarters I was sent on mission to Zhongshan and passed the peril of Jingxing Pass. Fearing the horse might stumble, I did not dare slacken the bridle;

units.zh: 及至平地，則無復持控，果為馬所顛仆，幾至於損。
units.en: but once I reached level ground I let go—and the horse threw me; I was nearly hurt.
units.literal: but once I reached level ground I no longer held control, and indeed the horse threw me—I was nearly injured.

units.zh: 臣所陳雖小，可以喻大。
units.en: What I tell is a small matter, but it stands for a large one.
units.literal: What I report is small, but it may illustrate what is great.

units.zh: 陛下勿以清晏豐熟，便縱逸樂，兢兢業業，臣之望也。」
units.en: Do not let peace and plenty lure you into ease and pleasure. Vigilance is what I ask of you."
units.literal: Your Majesty must not, because the realm is peaceful and the harvest rich, give way to ease and pleasure. Vigilant care—that is my hope.

units.zh: 明宗深然之。
units.en: Mingzong was deeply persuaded.
units.literal: Mingzong deeply approved.

units.zh: 他日又問道曰：「天下雖熟，百姓得濟否？」
units.en: On another day he asked Dao, "The harvest is good—but are the people actually better off?"
units.literal: Another day he asked Dao, "Though the realm has a good harvest, are the common people provided for?

units.zh: 道曰：「穀貴餓農，穀賤傷農，此常理也。
units.en: Dao said, "When grain is dear farmers go hungry; when grain is cheap farmers are ruined—that is the constant rule.
units.literal: Dao said, "When grain is dear the farmer starves; when grain is cheap the farmer is hurt—this is the constant rule.

units.zh: 臣憶得近代有舉子聶夷中《傷田家詩》云：『二月賣新絲，五月糶秋穀。
units.en: I recall a recent candidate, Nie Yizhong, who wrote in "Lament for a Farming Family": "In the second month I sell the new silk; in the fifth month I sell the autumn grain.
units.literal: I recall that in recent times the examination candidate Nie Yizhong wrote in his "Poem Lamenting the Farming Family": "In the second month I sell the new silk; in the fifth month I sell the autumn grain.

units.zh: 醫得眼下瘡，剜卻心頭肉。
units.en: To heal the sore before my eyes I cut out the flesh of my heart.
units.literal: To cure the sore before my eyes I gouge out the flesh of my heart.

units.zh: 我願君王心，化作光明燭。
units.en: I wish the ruler's heart were a bright candle,
units.literal: I wish the ruler's heart might become a bright shining candle,

units.zh: 不照綺羅筵，遍照逃亡屋。』」
units.en: not lighting brocade feasts but every fleeing household."
units.literal: not shining on brocade banquets but shining everywhere on the houses of the displaced."

units.zh: 明宗曰：「此詩甚好。」
units.en: Mingzong said, "That poem is excellent."
units.literal: Mingzong said, "This poem is excellent."

units.zh: 遂命侍臣錄下，每自諷之。
units.en: He had his attendants copy it and often recited it himself.
units.literal: He then ordered his attendants to copy it down, and he often recited it to himself.

units.zh: 道之發言簡正，善於裨益，非常人所能及也。
units.en: Dao spoke plainly and to the point and knew how to help—beyond what most men could do.
units.literal: Dao's words were concise and upright, and he excelled at offering benefit—beyond what ordinary men could match.

units.zh: 時以諸經舛繆，與同列李愚委學官田敏等，取西京鄭覃所刊石經，雕為印版，流布天下，後進賴之。
units.en: Because the classics were full of errors, he and his colleague Li Yu put the academic official Tian Min and others to taking Zheng Tan's stone classics from the Western Capital, cutting printing blocks, and spreading them across the realm—later students owed them a great debt.
units.literal: At the time the classics were full of errors. Together with his colleague Li Yu he entrusted the academic officials Tian Min and others to take the stone classics engraved by Zheng Tan in the Western Capital, cut them into printing blocks, and circulate them throughout the realm—later students relied on them.

units.zh: 明宗崩，唐末帝嗣位，以道為山陵使，禮畢，出鎮同州，循故事也。
units.en: When Mingzong died and the Last Emperor of Tang succeeded, Dao was made tomb commissioner; when the rites ended he was posted to Tongzhou as military governor, by established custom.
units.literal: When Mingzong died, the Last Emperor of Tang succeeded. Dao was made commissioner for the imperial tomb; when the rites were finished he was sent out to govern Tong Prefecture, following precedent.

units.zh: 道為政閑淡，獄市無撓。
units.en: His rule was relaxed and mild; prisons and markets were left in peace.
units.literal: Dao's administration was easy and mild; prisons and markets were undisturbed.

units.zh: 一日，有上介胡饒，本出軍吏，性粗獷，因事詬道於牙門，左右數報不應。
units.en: One day his senior aide Hu Rao, a former army clerk, coarse by nature, abused Dao at the gate over some affair. Attendants reported it again and again, but Dao did not respond.
units.literal: One day a senior aide, Hu Rao, originally a military clerk, coarse and fierce by nature, reviled Dao at the headquarters gate over some matter. His attendants reported it repeatedly, but he did not respond.

units.zh: 道曰：「此必醉耳！」
units.en: Dao said, "He must be drunk."
units.literal: Dao said, "He must be drunk!

units.zh: 因召入，開尊設食，盡夕而起，無撓慍之色。
units.en: He had him brought in, opened wine and set out a meal, and they sat until evening without a trace of anger.
units.literal: He then summoned him in, opened wine and set out food, and they remained until evening without a trace of annoyance on his face.

units.zh: 未幾，入為司空。
units.en: Soon he was recalled as Minister of Works.
units.literal: Before long he was recalled to serve as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 及晉祖入洛，以道為首相。
units.en: When Gaozu of Later Jin entered Luoyang he made Dao chief minister.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor of Jin entered Luoyang, he made Dao chief minister.

units.zh: 二年，契丹遣使加徽號於晉祖，晉祖亦獻徽號於契丹，謂道曰：「此行非卿不可。」
units.en: In the second year the Khitan sent envoys to bestow an honorific on Gaozu, and Gaozu in turn sent one to the Khitan. He told Dao, "No one but you can make this journey."
units.literal: In the second year the Khitan sent envoys to bestow an honorific title on the Jin founder, and the Jin founder also presented an honorific title to the Khitan. He told Dao, "This mission cannot be entrusted to anyone but you.

units.zh: 道無難色。
units.en: Dao showed no reluctance.
units.literal: Dao showed no sign of difficulty.

units.zh: 晉祖又曰：「卿官崇德重，不可深入沙漠。」
units.en: Gaozu added, "Your rank is high and your standing great—you must not go deep into the desert."
units.literal: The Jin founder added, "Your office is lofty and your virtue weighty—you must not penetrate deep into the desert.

units.zh: 道曰：「陛下受北朝恩，臣受陛下恩，何有不可！」
units.en: Dao said, "Your Majesty owes the northern court; I owe Your Majesty—what could I refuse?"
units.literal: Dao said, "Your Majesty received favor from the northern court; I received favor from Your Majesty—how could there be anything I could not do!"

units.zh: 〈（楊內翰《談苑》云：道與諸相歸中書，食訖，外廳堂吏前白道言北使事。
units.en: (Yang Neihan's Conversational Garden: Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat. After eating, a clerk of the outer hall came forward and told Dao about the northern mission.)
units.literal: (Yang Neihan's Conversational Garden says: Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat. After the meal, a clerk of the outer hall came forward and reported to Dao about the northern envoy mission.)

units.zh: 吏人色變手戰，道取紙一幅，署云：「道去。」
units.en: The clerk turned pale and his hands shook. Dao took a sheet of paper and wrote, "Dao will go."
units.literal: The clerk's face changed color and his hands trembled. Dao took a sheet of paper and wrote, "Dao will go.

units.zh: 即遣寫敕進，堂吏泣下。
units.en: He had an edict drafted and sent in at once; the hall clerk wept.
units.literal: He immediately had an edict drafted and submitted; the hall clerk wept.

units.zh: 道遣人語妻子，不復歸家，即日舍都亭驛，不數日北行。
units.en: He sent word to his wife and children that he would not come home, lodged that day at the Capital Pavilion relay, and within days marched north.
units.literal: Dao sent word to his wife and children that he would not return home, lodged that same day at the Capital Pavilion relay station, and within a few days set out north.

units.zh: 晉祖餞宴，語以家國之故，煩耆德遠使，自酌卮酒賜之，泣下。）〉
units.en: Gaozu gave a farewell feast, spoke of the needs of state and family, and said he was troubling an elder of virtue with a distant mission; he poured wine himself, gave it to Dao, and wept.)〉
units.literal: The Jin founder gave a farewell banquet, spoke of the needs of state and family, and said he was troubling an elder of virtue with a distant mission; he poured a cup of wine himself and bestowed it on him, weeping.)〉

units.zh: 及行，將達西樓，契丹主欲郊迎，其臣曰：「天子無迎宰相之禮。」
units.en: As he traveled and neared the Western Tower, the Khitan ruler wished to welcome him with suburban rites. His ministers said, "The Son of Heaven does not go out to welcome a chief minister."
units.literal: When he traveled and was about to reach the Western Tower, the Khitan ruler wished to welcome him with suburban rites. His ministers said, "The Son of Heaven has no rite of welcoming a chief minister.

units.zh: 因止焉，其名動殊俗也如此。
units.en: So they stopped him—such was the power of his name among foreign peoples.
units.literal: They therefore stopped him—such was the way his fame stirred foreign peoples.

units.zh: 〈（《談苑》云：契丹賜其臣牙笏及臘日賜牛頭者為殊禮，道皆得之，作詩以紀曰：「牛頭偏得賜，象笏更容持。」
units.en: (Conversational Garden: Among the Khitan, ivory tablets for ministers and ox heads on the La festival were special honors. Dao received both and wrote: "The ox head fell to me alone; the ivory tablet I may hold as well.")
units.literal: (Conversational Garden says: Among the Khitan, bestowing ivory tablets on ministers and giving ox heads on the La festival day were special honors. Dao received both and wrote a poem to record it: "The ox head I alone was granted; the ivory tablet I may also hold.")

units.zh: 契丹主甚喜，遂潛諭留意，道曰：「南朝為子，北朝為父，兩朝皆為臣，豈有分別哉！」
units.en: The Khitan ruler was delighted and quietly urged him to stay. Dao said, "The southern court is the son, the northern court the father—yet I am subject to both courts. What difference is there?"
units.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and secretly instructed him to consider staying. Dao said, "The southern court is son, the northern court is father—both are courts to which I am subject. How could there be any distinction!"

units.zh: 道在契丹，凡得所賜，悉以市薪炭，征其意，云：「北地苦寒，老年所不堪，當為之備。」
units.en: In Khitan lands he spent every gift on firewood and coal, hinting, "The northern country is bitterly cold, unbearable for an old man; I must prepare for it"—as if he meant to stay.
units.literal: While Dao was among the Khitan, whatever gifts he received he used entirely to buy firewood and coal, hinting at his intent: "The north is bitterly cold—more than an old man can bear; I must prepare for it."

units.zh: 若將久留者。
units.en: He acted as though he meant to remain for good.
units.literal: It was as if he intended to remain long.

units.zh: 契丹感其意，乃遣歸，道三上表乞留，固遣乃去，猶更住館中月餘。
units.en: Moved, the Khitan sent him home. Dao submitted three memorials begging to stay; only when they firmly dismissed him did he leave—and he still lodged at the guest house for more than a month.
units.literal: The Khitan, moved by his intent, then sent him back. Dao submitted three memorials begging to stay; only when they firmly sent him off did he leave, yet he still lodged at the guest house for more than a month.

units.zh: 既行，所至留駐，凡兩月方出境，左右語道曰：「當北土得生還，恨無羽翼，公獨宿留，何也？」
units.en: On the road he halted at every stop and took two months to cross the border. His attendants said, "Men who escape the north wish they had wings—yet you linger. Why?"
units.literal: Once he set out, he halted wherever he went and spent two full months before leaving the border. His attendants said to Dao, "To escape the north alive, one regrets having no wings—yet you alone linger. Why?

units.zh: 道曰：「縱急還，彼以筋腳馬，一夕即追及，亦何可脫，但徐緩即不能測矣。」
units.en: Dao said, "Even if we hurry, their swift horses would overtake us in a night—how could we escape? Go slowly and they cannot read our intent."
units.literal: Dao said, "Even if we hurry back, they have swift horses and would overtake us in a single night—how could we escape? Only by going slowly can they not guess our intent."

units.zh: 眾乃服。
units.en: His men were convinced.
units.literal: The company then submitted to his reasoning.

units.zh: 四年二月，始至京師。）〉
units.en: In the second month of the fourth year he finally reached the capital.)〉
units.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he finally reached the capital.)〉

units.zh: 及還，朝廷廢樞密使，依唐朝故事，並歸中書，其院印付道，事無巨細，悉以歸之。
units.en: On his return the court abolished the Bureau of Military Affairs; following Tang precedent its duties reverted to the Secretariat, the bureau seal went to Dao, and every matter great or small was left to him.
units.literal: When he returned, the court abolished the office of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; following Tang precedent, its duties all reverted to the Secretariat, and the bureau's seal was handed to Dao. Matters great and small were entirely entrusted to him.

units.zh: 尋加司徒、兼侍中，進魯國公。
units.en: Soon he was made Minister of Education (Situ) and concurrent Palace Attendant and advanced to Duke of Lu.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Minister of Education (Situ) and concurrent Palace Attendant, advanced to Duke of Lu.

units.zh: 晉祖曾以用兵事問道，道曰：「陛下歷試諸艱，創成大業，神武睿略，為天下所知，討伐不庭，須從獨斷。
units.en: Gaozu once asked Dao about war. Dao said, "Your Majesty has endured every trial and built a great enterprise. Your martial genius is known to all. In punishing rebels you must decide alone.
units.literal: The Jin founder once asked Dao about military affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty has passed through every hardship and founded a great enterprise. Your divine martial prowess and wise strategy are known throughout the realm. In punishing the recalcitrant, you must rely on your own sole judgment."

units.zh: 臣本自書生，為陛下在中書，守歷代成規，不敢有一毫之失也。」
units.en: I began as a scholar; in the Secretariat I keep the rules of past dynasties and dare not stray by a hair."
units.literal: I began as a mere scholar; serving Your Majesty in the Secretariat, I keep the established rules of successive dynasties and dare not err by a hair's breadth."

units.zh: 臣在明宗朝，曾以戎事問臣，臣亦以斯言答之。」
units.en: Under Mingzong he asked me the same question, and I gave the same answer."
units.literal: In Emperor Mingzong's court he once asked me about military affairs, and I answered with these same words."

units.zh: 晉祖頗可其說。
units.en: Gaozu largely approved.
units.literal: The Jin founder largely approved his view.

units.zh: 道嘗上表求退，晉祖不之覽，先遣鄭王就省，謂曰：「卿來日不出，朕當親行請卿。」
units.en: Dao once asked to retire. Gaozu did not read the memorial but sent the Prince of Zheng to visit him, saying, "If you do not come out tomorrow, I will come in person to fetch you."
units.literal: Dao once submitted a memorial requesting retirement. The Jin founder did not read it but first sent the Prince of Zheng to visit him, saying, "If you do not come out tomorrow, I shall go in person to invite you.

units.zh: 道不得已出焉。
units.en: Dao had no choice but to return to office.
units.literal: Dao had no choice but to go out.

units.zh: 當時寵遇，無與為比。
units.en: At the time no one enjoyed such favor.
units.literal: At the time his favor and treatment had no equal.

units.zh: 晉少帝即位，加守太尉，進封燕國公。
units.en: When the Young Emperor of Later Jin succeeded, Dao was made acting Grand Commandant and Duke of Yan.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor of Jin succeeded, Dao was made acting Grand Commandant and advanced to Duke of Yan.

units.zh: 道嘗問朝中熟客曰：「道之在政事堂，人有何說？」
units.en: Dao once asked a court acquaintance, "What do people say about me in the Hall of Administration?"
units.literal: Dao once asked a familiar guest at court, "What do people say about me in the Hall of Administration?

units.zh: 客曰：「是非相半。」
units.en: The guest said, "Opinion is evenly split."
units.literal: The guest said, "Praise and blame are evenly divided."

units.zh: 道曰：「凡人同者為是，不同為非，而非道者，十恐有九。
units.en: Dao said, "Men call agreement right and disagreement wrong—and I daresay nine in ten call me wrong.
units.literal: Dao said, "Ordinary men call what agrees with them right and what differs wrong—and of those who call me wrong, I fear nine in ten.

units.zh: 昔仲尼聖人也，猶為叔孫武叔所毀，況道之虛薄者乎！」
units.en: Confucius himself was slandered by Shusun Wushu—what of someone as slight as me!"
units.literal: In antiquity Confucius was a sage, yet he was still slandered by Shusun Wushu—how much more one as empty and slight as I!"

units.zh: 然道之所持，始終不易。
units.en: Yet Dao never changed what he held to from first to last.
units.literal: Yet what Dao held to he never changed from beginning to end.

units.zh: 後有人間道於少帝曰：「道好平時宰相，無以濟其艱難，如禪僧不可呼鷹耳！」
units.en: Later someone told the Young Emperor, "Dao is a peacetime minister who cannot meet crisis—like a Chan monk who cannot hunt with hawks!"
units.literal: Later someone slandered Dao to the Young Emperor, saying, "Dao is suited to be chief minister in peaceful times but cannot meet hard times—like a Chan monk who cannot call hawks!

units.zh: 由是出道為同州節度使。
units.en: For this Dao was posted out as military governor of Tongzhou.
units.literal: For this reason Dao was sent out as military governor of Tong Prefecture.

units.zh: 歲餘，移鎮南陽，加中書令。
units.en: After a year he was transferred to Nanyang and made Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to govern Nanyang and made Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 契丹入汴，道自襄、鄧召入，戎王因從容問曰：「天下百姓，如何可救？」
units.en: When the Khitan took Bian, Dao was summoned from Xiang and Deng. The Khitan ruler asked him casually, "How can the people of the realm be saved?"
units.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Dao was summoned from Xiang and Deng. The foreign ruler asked him at ease, "How can the common people of the realm be saved?

units.zh: 道曰：「此時百姓，佛再出救不得，惟皇帝救得。」
units.en: Dao said, "At this hour not even the Buddha reborn could save them—only the emperor can."
units.literal: Dao said, "At this time the common people—even if the Buddha were born again he could not save them; only the emperor can save them."

units.zh: 其後衣冠不至傷夷，皆道與趙延壽陰護之所至也。
units.en: Afterward the gentry were spared harm—thanks to the secret protection of Dao and Zhao Yanshou.
units.literal: Afterward the gentry and officials were not harmed—this was entirely due to the secret protection of Dao and Zhao Yanshou.

units.zh: 是歲三月，隨契丹北行，與晉室公卿俱抵常山。
units.en: That March he marched north with the Khitan and reached Changshan with the Jin court.
units.literal: That year in the third month he traveled north with the Khitan and, together with the chief ministers of the Jin court, reached Changshan.

units.zh: 俄而戎王卒，永康王代統其眾。
units.en: Soon the Khitan ruler died and the Prince of Yongkang took command of his forces.
units.literal: Shortly afterward the Khitan ruler died, and the Prince of Yongkang succeeded to command of his forces.

units.zh: 及北去，留其族嘉裏以據常山。
units.en: On the march north they left their clansman Jiali to hold Changshan.
units.literal: When they went north they left their clansman Jiali to hold Changshan.

units.zh: 時漢軍憤激，因共逐出嘉裏，尋復其城。
units.en: The Han troops, furious, drove Jiali out and soon retook the city.
units.literal: At the time the Han troops were inflamed with anger and together drove Jiali out, soon recovering the city.

units.zh: 道率同列四出按撫，因事從宜，各安其所。
units.en: Dao led his colleagues out in all directions to pacify the people, adapting to circumstances until each was settled.
units.literal: Dao led his colleagues in all directions to reassure and pacify, adapting measures to circumstances so that each settled in his place.

units.zh: 人或推其功，道曰：「儒臣何能為，皆諸將之力也。」
units.en: When men praised his achievement, Dao said, "What could a scholar-official do? It was all the generals' work."
units.literal: When some praised his achievement, Dao said, "What could a Confucian minister do? It was all the generals' strength.

units.zh: 道以德重，人所取則，乃為眾擇諸將之勤宿者，以騎校白再榮權為其帥，軍民由是帖然，道首有力焉。
units.en: Because men looked to his moral weight, he chose the most seasoned generals and made the cavalry officer Bai Zairong acting commander. Army and people settled down, and Dao was chiefly responsible.
units.literal: Because Dao's virtue was weighty and men took him as their model, he chose for the company the most diligent and seasoned of the generals and made the cavalry officer Bai Zairong acting commander. Army and people were thereby settled, and Dao was foremost in bringing this about.

units.zh: 道在常山，見有中國士女為契丹所俘者，出橐裝以贖之，皆寄於高尼精舍，後相次訪其家以歸之。
units.en: At Changshan he saw Chinese men and women taken by the Khitan; he paid from his purse to ransom them, lodged them at a nunnery, and later found their families and sent them home.
units.literal: While Dao was at Changshan he saw Chinese men and women taken captive by the Khitan; he spent from his purse to redeem them, lodged them all at a nunnery of eminent nuns, and later sought out their families one after another to return them.

units.zh: 又，契丹先留道與李崧、和凝及文武官等在常山，是歲閏七月二十九日，契丹有詔追崧，令選朝士十人赴木葉山行事。
units.en: The Khitan had left Dao with Li Song, He Ning, and the rest at Changshan. On the twenty-ninth of the intercalary seventh month the Khitan summoned Song and ordered ten court scholars chosen for service at Mount Muye.
units.literal: Moreover, the Khitan had earlier left Dao with Li Song, He Ning, and the civil and military officials at Changshan. On the twenty-ninth day of the intercalary seventh month that year the Khitan issued an edict summoning Song and ordering the selection of ten court scholars to go to Mount Muye for state business.

units.zh: 契丹麻答召道等至帳所，欲諭之，崧偶先至，知其意，懼形於色。
units.en: The Khitan Maduo summoned them to his tent. Song arrived first, guessed his intent, and fear showed on his face.
units.literal: The Khitan Maduo summoned Dao and the others to his tent to instruct them. Song happened to arrive first, understood his intent, and fear showed on his face.

units.zh: 契丹麻答將以明日與朝士齊遣之，崧乃不俟道，與凝先出，既而相遇於帳門之外，因與分手俱歸。
units.en: Maduo meant to send them off with the court scholars the next day. Song left without waiting for Dao, together with He Ning; they met outside the tent, parted, and went home together.
units.literal: Maduo intended to send him off the next day together with the court scholars. Song therefore did not wait for Dao but left first with He Ning; they met outside the tent gate, bade farewell, and returned together.

units.zh: 俄而李筠等縱火與契丹交鬥，鼓槊相及。
units.en: Soon Li Yun and others set fires and fought the Khitan hand to hand.
units.literal: Shortly afterward Li Yun and others set fires and fought the Khitan; drums and spears clashed.

units.zh: 是日若齊至，與麻答相見，稍或躊躇，則悉為俘矣。
units.en: Had they all arrived that day and met Maduo, the slightest hesitation would have made captives of them all.
units.literal: If they had all arrived together that day and met Maduo, and had hesitated even slightly, they would all have been taken captive.

units.zh: 時論者以道布衣有至行，立公朝有重望，其陰報昭感，多此類也。
units.en: Commentators held that Dao, a commoner of supreme conduct who commanded great respect at court, received many such hidden rewards and manifest responses.
units.literal: Commentators of the time held that Dao, though a commoner in origin, had supreme conduct, and once established in the public court possessed great standing; his hidden rewards and manifest responses were mostly of this kind.

units.zh: 及自常山入覲，漢祖嘉之，拜守太師。
units.en: When he came from Changshan to court, Gaozu of Later Han commended him and made him acting Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When he came from Changshan to pay court, the Founding Emperor of Han commended him and appointed him acting Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 〈（《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》：贈大監張公璨，漢祖即位之初為上黨戎判。
units.en: (Old Hearings among the Gentry of Luoyang: Zhang Gongcan, posthumously Grand Director, was military judge at Shangdang early in Gaozu's reign.)
units.literal: (Old Hearings among the Gentry of Luoyang: Zhang Gongcan, posthumously Grand Director, served early in the Han founder's reign as military judge at Shangdang.)

units.zh: 漢祖在北京時，大聚甲兵，禁牛皮不得私貿易及民間盜用之，如有牛死，即時官納其皮，其有犯者甚眾。
units.en: When Gaozu was at Beijing he massed armor and troops and banned private trade in ox hides; any dead ox's hide had to be turned in at once. Violations were countless.
units.literal: When the Han founder was at Beijing he gathered armor and troops in great numbers and forbade private trade in ox hides and their theft for private use among the people. If an ox died, its hide had to be turned in to the government at once. Very many violated the rule.

units.zh: 及即大位，三司舉行請禁天下牛皮法，與河東時同，天下苦之。
units.en: On taking the throne the Three Departments proposed enforcing the hide ban empire-wide as in Hedong, and the realm groaned under it.
units.literal: When he took the throne, the Three Departments proposed enforcing the prohibition on ox hides throughout the realm, the same as in Hedong times, and the realm suffered under it.

units.zh: 會上黨民犯牛皮者二十餘人，獄成，罪俱當死。
units.en: More than twenty Shangdang men violated the hide law; their cases were closed and all faced death.
units.literal: More than twenty people at Shangdang violated the hide law; the cases were concluded and all were sentenced to death.

units.zh: 大監時為判官，獨執曰：「主上欽明，三司不合如此起請，二十餘人死尚間可，使天下犯者皆銜冤而死乎！
units.en: Zhang, then judge, alone objected: "Our lord is discerning; the Three Departments should not propose this. Twenty deaths might be bearable—but shall every violator in the realm die wrongfully?
units.literal: The Grand Director, then serving as judge, alone held firm and said, "Our lord is discerning; the Three Departments ought not to propose such a measure. The death of twenty-odd men might still be tolerable—but are all violators throughout the realm to die bearing wrongful grievance!

units.zh: 且主上在河東，大聚甲兵，須藉牛皮，嚴禁可也，今為天下君，何少牛皮，立法至於此乎！」
units.en: In Hedong he needed hides for armor—a strict ban made sense. Now he rules the realm—what shortage of hides requires law this harsh?"
units.literal: Moreover, when our lord was in Hedong he gathered armor and troops in great numbers and needed ox hides—a strict ban was fitting. Now that he is ruler of the realm, what shortage of hides is there that law should go to such lengths!

units.zh: 遂封奏之。
units.en: He sealed and submitted a memorial.
units.literal: He then sealed and submitted a memorial.

units.zh: 時三司使方用事，執政之地，除馮瀛王外皆惡之，曰：「豈有州郡使敢非朝廷詔敕！」
units.en: The Three Departments were in power; everyone in government except the Prince of Ying hated him and said, "How dare a prefectural commissioner oppose an imperial edict!"
units.literal: At the time the commissioners of the Three Departments were in power; in the seats of government all except the Prince of Ying hated him and said, "How can a prefectural commissioner dare oppose an imperial edict of the court!

units.zh: 力言於漢祖。
units.en: They pressed Gaozu hard.
units.literal: They spoke forcefully to the Han founder.

units.zh: 漢祖亦怒曰：「昭義一判官，是何敢如此！
units.en: Gaozu was furious: "A mere judge of Zhaoyi—how dare he!
units.literal: The Han founder was also angry and said, "A single judge of Zhaoyi—how dare he do this!

units.zh: 其犯牛皮者，依敕俱死。
units.en: Let every violator die as the edict commands.
units.literal: Those who violated the hide law shall all die according to the edict.

units.zh: 大監以非毀詔敕，亦死。」
units.en: Zhang, for denouncing the edict, shall die as well."
units.literal: The Grand Director, for denouncing the edict, shall also die.

units.zh: 敕未下，獨瀛王非時請見。
units.en: Before the edict issued, the Prince of Ying alone sought an unscheduled audience.
units.literal: Before the edict was issued, the Prince of Ying alone requested an audience at an irregular hour.

units.zh: 漢祖出，瀛王曰：「陛下在河東時，斷牛皮可也，今既有天下，牛皮不合禁。
units.en: When Gaozu came out, the Prince of Ying said, "In Hedong a hide ban was fitting; now that you rule the realm, hides should not be banned.
units.literal: When the Han founder came out, the Prince of Ying said, "When Your Majesty was in Hedong, prohibiting ox hides was fitting; now that you possess the realm, hides ought not to be banned.

units.zh: 陛下赤子枉死之，亦足為陛下惜。
units.en: Your people would die wrongfully—that alone is reason to grieve for you.
units.literal: Your Majesty's common people would die wrongfully—this is enough to make one grieve for Your Majesty.

units.zh: 昭義判官，以卑位食陛下祿，居陛下官，不惜軀命，敢執而奏之，可賞不可殺。
units.en: The Zhaoyi judge, in a humble post on your salary, risked his life to memorialize—he should be rewarded, not executed.
units.literal: The judge of Zhaoyi, in a humble post eating Your Majesty's salary and holding Your Majesty's office, did not spare his life but dared to hold firm and memorialize—he should be rewarded, not killed.

units.zh: 臣當輔弼之任，使此敕枉害天下人性命，臣不能早奏，使陛下正，臣罪當誅。」
units.en: I hold the duty of counselor; that this edict would wrongfully kill people across the realm—I failed to speak early and set you right. My crime deserves death."
units.literal: I bear the duty of assisting and supporting; that this edict should wrongfully harm the lives of people throughout the realm—I failed to memorialize early and set Your Majesty right. My crime deserves execution.

units.zh: 稽首再拜。
units.en: He kowtowed twice.
units.literal: He bowed his head and prostrated himself twice.

units.zh: 又曰：「張璨不合加罪，望加敕赦之。」
units.en: He added, "Zhang Can should not be punished—I beg an edict to pardon him."
units.literal: He added, "Zhang Can ought not to be punished; I hope an edict will pardon him.

units.zh: 漢祖久之曰：「已行之矣。」
units.en: After a long pause Gaozu said, "It has already been done."
units.literal: After a long silence the Han founder said, "It has already been carried out."

units.zh: 馮瀛王曰：「敕未下。」
units.en: The Prince of Ying said, "The edict has not gone out."
units.literal: The Prince of Ying said, "The edict has not yet been issued."

units.zh: 漢祖遽曰：「與赦之。」
units.en: Gaozu said quickly, "Pardon them."
units.literal: The Han founder said hastily, "Pardon them."

units.zh: 馮曰：「勒停可乎？」
units.en: Feng said, "Would halting it suffice?"
units.literal: Feng said, "Would ordering it halted suffice?"

units.zh: 上曰：「可。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Yes."
units.literal: The emperor said, "It will do."

units.zh: 由是改其敕，記其略曰：「三司邦計，國法攸依，張璨體事未明，執理乖當，宜停見職，犯牛皮者貸命放之。」
units.en: The edict was changed to read in substance: "The Three Departments manage state finance. Zhang Can misunderstood the matter and handled it wrongly; remove him from office. Spare the hide-law violators and release them."
units.literal: Thereupon the edict was changed; its gist recorded: "The Three Departments manage state finance and national law is what they rely on. Zhang Can did not understand the matter clearly and his handling of principle was improper; he should be removed from his current post. Those who violated the hide law are spared death and released."

units.zh: 大監聽宣敕訖，聞敕云「執理乖當」，尚曰：「中書自不能執理，若一一教外道判官執理，則焉用彼相乎！」）〉
units.en: When Zhang heard the edict read and the phrase "handling of principle was improper," he still said, "If the Secretariat cannot handle principle and every provincial judge must do it, what are chief ministers for!" )〉
units.literal: When the Grand Director heard the edict proclaimed and heard the words "handling of principle was improper," he still said, "If the Secretariat itself cannot handle principle and must teach every outer-circuit judge to handle principle, what use are those chief ministers!" )〉

units.zh: 乾祐中，道奉朝請外，平居自適。
units.en: During Qianyou Dao attended court when required but otherwise lived at ease.
units.literal: During the Qianyou era Dao attended court when summoned but otherwise lived at ease in ordinary times.

units.zh: 一日，著《長樂老自敘》云：
units.en: One day he wrote his "Autobiography of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy," which reads:
units.literal: One day he composed his "Autobiographical Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy," which reads:

units.zh: 余世家宗族，本始平、長樂二郡，歷代之名實，具載於國史家牒。
units.en: My clan for generations has roots in Shiping and Changle; each generation's record is in the histories and family registers.
units.literal: My clan and family for generations have their roots in the two commanderies of Shiping and Changle; the names and facts of each generation are fully recorded in the national histories and family registers.

units.zh: 余先自燕亡歸晉，事莊宗、明宗、閔帝、清泰帝，又事晉高祖皇帝、少帝。
units.en: I fled Yan's fall to Jin and served Zhuangzong, Mingzong, Min, and Qingtai, then Gaozu and the Young Emperor of Later Jin.
units.literal: I first fled Yan's fall and returned to Jin, serving Emperor Zhuangzong, Emperor Mingzong, Emperor Min, and Emperor Qingtai, and then serving the Founding Emperor of Jin and the Young Emperor.

units.zh: 契丹據汴京，為北主所制，自鎮州與文武臣僚、馬步將士歸漢朝，事高祖皇帝、今上。
units.en: When the Khitan held Bian, I was held by the northern ruler; from Zhenzhou I returned to Han with officials and troops and now serve Gaozu and the present emperor.
units.literal: When the Khitan held Bianjing I was constrained by the northern ruler; from Zhen Prefecture I returned to the Han court with civil and military officials and horse and foot troops, serving the Founding Emperor and the present sovereign.

units.zh: 顧以久叨祿位，備歷艱危，上顯祖宗，下光親戚。
units.en: Long enjoying rank and passing through every trial, I have honored my ancestors above and my kin below.
units.literal: Reflecting that I have long enjoyed salary and rank and have passed through every hardship, I have brought honor above to my ancestors and glory below to my kin.

units.zh: 亡曾祖諱湊，累贈至太傅，亡曾祖母崔氏，追封梁國太夫人；
units.en: My late great-grandfather Cou was posthumously made Grand Tutor; my late great-grandmother, née Cui, Grand Lady of Liang;
units.literal: My deceased great-grandfather, personal name Cou, was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor; my deceased great-grandmother, née Cui, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Liang;

units.zh: 亡祖諱炯，累贈至太師，亡祖母褚氏，追封吳國太夫人；
units.en: my late grandfather Jiong, Grand Preceptor; my late grandmother, née Chu, Grand Lady of Wu;
units.literal: my deceased grandfather, personal name Jiong, was posthumously advanced to Grand Preceptor; my deceased grandmother, née Chu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Wu;

units.zh: 亡父諱良建，秘書少監致仕，累贈至尚書令，母張氏，追封魏國太夫人。
units.en: my late father Liangjian, retired Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumously Director of the Department of State Affairs; my mother, née Zhang, Grand Lady of Wei.
units.literal: my deceased father, personal name Liangjian, retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was posthumously advanced to Director of the Department of State Affairs; my mother, née Zhang, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Wei.

units.zh: 余階自將仕郎，轉朝議郎、朝散大夫、銀青光祿大夫、金紫光祿大夫、特進、開府儀同三司。
units.en: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit through court grand master titles to Special Advancement and Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
units.literal: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Discussion, Grand Master for Court Assembly, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal, Special Advancement, and Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

units.zh: 職自幽州節度巡官、河東節度巡官、掌書記，再為翰林學士，改授端明殿學士、集賢殿大學士、太微宮使，再為宏文館大學士，又充諸道鹽鐵轉運使、南郊大禮使、明宗皇帝晉高祖皇帝山陵使，再授定國軍節度、同州管內觀察處置等使，一為長春宮使，又授武勝軍節度、鄧隨均房等州管內觀察處置等使。
units.en: My posts ran from Youzhou and Hedong inspector to chief secretary; twice Hanlin academician; then academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Taiwei Palace commissioner, and Hongwen grand academician; also salt-and-iron transport commissioner, southern suburban rites commissioner, and tomb commissioner for Mingzong and Gaozu of Jin; twice military governor of the Dingguo army and Tongzhou observation commissioner; once Everlasting Spring Palace commissioner; and military governor of the Wusheng army with observation over Deng, Sui, Jun, Fang, and other prefectures.
units.literal: My posts ran from inspector of the Youzhou military commission and inspector of the Hedong military commission to chief secretary; twice Hanlin Academician; then Academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Commissioner of the Taiwei Palace; again Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute; also Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport of all circuits, Commissioner for the Southern Suburban Grand Rites, and Commissioner for the imperial tombs of Emperor Mingzong and the Founding Emperor of Jin; twice military governor of the Dingguo Army and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition within Tong Prefecture; once Commissioner of the Everlasting Spring Palace; and again military governor of the Wusheng Army and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition within Deng, Sui, Jun, Fang, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 官自攝幽府參軍、試大理評事、檢校尚書祠部郎中兼侍御史、檢校吏部郎中兼御史中丞、檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事、檢校太師、兼侍中，又授檢校太師、兼中書令。
units.en: My offices ran from acting Youzhou aide and probationary judicial reviewer through acting ministry directors with censorial posts to acting Grand Commandant, Grand Councilor, acting Grand Preceptor with Palace Attendant, and again acting Grand Preceptor with Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: My offices ran from acting aide in the You prefectural staff, probationary reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, acting Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices in the Ministry of Rites with concurrent Attending Censor, acting Director in the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, acting Grand Commandant, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, acting Grand Preceptor with concurrent Palace Attendant, and again acting Grand Preceptor with concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 正官自行臺中書舍人，再為戶部侍郎，轉兵部侍郎、中書侍郎，再為門下侍郎、刑部吏部尚書、右僕射，三為司空，兩在中書，一守本官，又授司徒、兼侍中，賜私門十六戟，又授太尉、兼侍中，又授戎太傅，又授漢太師。
units.en: My regular offices ran from Secretariat drafting secretary to twice Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Ministers of War and Secretariat, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Ministers of Justice and Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thrice Minister of Works, twice in the Secretariat and once keeping the original office; then Minister of Education (Situ) with Palace Attendant, sixteen halberds for my gate, Grand Commandant with Palace Attendant, Khitan Grand Tutor, and Han Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: My regular offices ran from Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat to twice Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Minister of War and Vice Director of the Secretariat, again Vice Director of the Chancellery, Minister of Justice and Minister of Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thrice Minister of Works, twice in the Secretariat, once keeping my original office; then Grand Mentor with concurrent Palace Attendant, granted sixteen halberds for my private gate, then Grand Commandant with concurrent Palace Attendant, then Khitan Grand Tutor, then Han Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 爵自開國男至開國公、魯國公，再封秦國公、梁國公、燕國公、齊國公。
units.en: My titles ran from founding viscount to founding duke and Duke of Lu, then Duke of Qin, Liang, Yan, and Qi.
units.literal: My nobility ran from Viscount Who Establishes the State to Duke Who Establishes the State and Duke of Lu, then enfeoffed as Duke of Qin, Duke of Liang, Duke of Yan, and Duke of Qi.

units.zh: 食邑自三百戶至一萬一千戶，食實封自一百戶至一千八百戶。
units.en: My nominal fief ran from three hundred to eleven thousand households; my actual fief from one hundred to eighteen hundred.
units.literal: My fief households ran from three hundred to eleven thousand; my actual fief households from one hundred to eighteen hundred.

units.zh: 勛自柱國至上柱國。
units.en: My orders of merit ran from Pillar of the State to Supreme Pillar.
units.literal: My orders of merit ran from Pillar of the State to Supreme Pillar of the State.

units.zh: 功臣名自經邦致理翊贊功臣至守正崇德保邦致理功臣、安時處順守義崇靜功臣、崇仁保德寧邦翊聖功臣。
units.en: My merit titles ran from "Orders the State and Brings Order" through "Upholds Rectitude and Preserves the State" and "Keeps the Times and Upholds Righteousness" to "Honors Benevolence and Pacifies the State."
units.literal: My merit titles ran from Merit Subject Who Orders the State and Brings Order through Merit Subject Who Upholds Rectitude, Honors Virtue, and Preserves the State and Brings Order, Merit Subject Who Keeps the Times, Abides in Accord, Upholds Righteousness, and Honors Tranquility, to Merit Subject Who Honors Benevolence, Preserves Virtue, Pacifies the State, and Assists the Sage.

units.zh: 先娶故德州戶掾褚諱濆女，早亡，後娶故景州弓高縣孫明府諱師禮女，累封蜀國夫人。
units.en: I first married the daughter of the late Chu Fen, clerk of Dezhou, who died young; later I married the daughter of the late Sun Shili, magistrate of Gonggao, enfeoffed as Lady of Shu.
units.literal: I first married the daughter of Chu Fen, deceased clerk of household registers in De Prefecture, who died early; later I married the daughter of Sun Shili, deceased magistrate of Gonggao County in Jing Prefecture, who was repeatedly enfeoffed as Lady of Shu.

units.zh: 亡長子平，自秘書郎授右拾遺、工部度支員外郎；
units.en: My late eldest son Ping, from Secretariat secretary to Right Reminder and Vice Director of Revenue Accounts;
units.literal: My deceased eldest son Ping, from Secretary of the Secretariat appointed Right Reminder and Vice Director of Revenue Accounts in the Ministry of Works;

units.zh: 次子吉，自秘書省校書郎授膳部金部職方員外郎、屯田郎中；
units.en: my second son Ji, from Secretariat collator to vice director in several boards and director in the Board of State Farms;
units.literal: my second son Ji, from Collator in the Secretariat appointed Vice Director in the Boards of Provisions, Revenue, and Personnel and Director in the Board of State Farms;

units.zh: 第三亡子可，自秘書省正字授殿中丞、工部戶部員外郎；
units.en: my late third son Ke, from Secretariat proofreader to Palace Vice Director and vice director in Works and Revenue;
units.literal: my third deceased son Ke, from Proofreader in the Secretariat appointed Palace Vice Director and Vice Director in the Ministries of Works and Revenue;

units.zh: 第四子幼亡；
units.en: my fourth son died young;
units.literal: my fourth son died in youth;

units.zh: 第五子義，自秘書郎改授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼御史中丞，充定國軍衙內都指揮使，職罷改授朝散大夫、左春坊太子司議郎、授太常丞；
units.en: my fifth son Yi, from secretary to silver-seal grand master, acting chancellor of education with Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Dingguo headquarters commander; later court grand master, heir-apparent discussion master, and Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices;
units.literal: my fifth son Yi, from Secretary appointed Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, acting Chancellor of the Directorate of Education with concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Commander-in-Chief within the headquarters of the Dingguo Army; when that post ended, appointed Grand Master for Court Assembly, Master of Discussion in the Left Spring Palace of the Heir Apparent, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

units.zh: 第六子正，自協律郎改授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼御史中丞，充定國軍節度使，職罷改授朝散大夫、太僕丞。
units.en: my sixth son Zheng, from master of harmonics to silver-seal grand master, acting education chancellor with Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Dingguo military governor; later court grand master and Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
units.literal: my sixth son Zheng, from Master of Harmonics appointed Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, acting Chancellor of the Directorate of Education with concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of the Dingguo Army; when that post ended, appointed Grand Master for Court Assembly and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

units.zh: 長女適故兵部崔侍郎諱衍子太僕少卿名絢，封萬年縣君；
units.en: My eldest daughter married Xuan, son of the late Vice Minister Cui Yan, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, and was Lady of Wannian County;
units.literal: My eldest daughter married Xuan, son of the deceased Vice Minister of War Cui Yan; Xuan was Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, and she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wannian County;

units.zh: 三女子早亡。
units.en: three daughters died young.
units.literal: three daughters died early.

units.zh: 二孫幼亡。
units.en: Two grandsons died young.
units.literal: Two grandsons died in youth.

units.zh: 唐長興二年敕，瀛州景城縣莊來蘇鄉改為元輔鄉，朝漢裏為孝行裏。
units.en: By edict in Changxing 2, Laisu Township in Jingcheng, Yingzhou, became Yuanfu Township and Chaohan Lane became Xiaoxing Lane.
units.literal: By edict in the second year of Changxing of Tang, Laisu Township in Jingcheng County, Ying Prefecture, was renamed Yuanfu Township, and Chaohan Lane was renamed Xiaoxing Lane.

units.zh: 洛南莊貫河南府洛陽縣三州鄉靈臺裏，奉晉天福五年敕，三州鄉改為上相鄉，靈臺裏改為中臺裏，時守司徒、兼侍中；
units.en: My Luonan estate lay in Lingtai Lane, Sanzhou Township, Luoyang. By Tianfu 5 edict, Sanzhou became Shangxiang Township and Lingtai became Zhongtai Lane, when I was Grand Mentor with Palace Attendant;
units.literal: My estate south of Luo lay in Lingtai Lane, Sanzhou Township, Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture. By edict in the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, Sanzhou Township was renamed Shangxiang Township and Lingtai Lane was renamed Zhongtai Lane, when I held the posts of Grand Mentor with concurrent Palace Attendant;

units.zh: 又奉八年敕，上相鄉改為太尉鄉，中臺裏改為侍中裏，時守太尉、兼侍中。
units.en: by the eighth-year edict, Shangxiang became Taiwei Township and Zhongtai became Shizhong Lane, when I was Grand Commandant with Palace Attendant.
units.literal: again by edict in the eighth year, Shangxiang Township was renamed Taiwei Township and Zhongtai Lane was renamed Shizhong Lane, when I held the posts of Grand Commandant with concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 靜思本末，慶及存亡，蓋自國恩，盡從家法，承訓誨之旨，關教化之源，在孝於家，在忠於國，口無不道之言，門無不義之貨。
units.en: Reflecting on my life, my blessings reach living and dead—from the state's grace and my family's law. I took instruction to heart, the root of civilization: filial at home, loyal to the state; no improper word, no ill-gotten goods at my door.
units.literal: Reflecting quietly on root and branch, my blessings reach the living and the dead—all from the state's grace, all following the family's law. I received the aim of instruction and teaching, which touches the source of transformation: filial at home, loyal to the state; no improper word from my mouth, no unrighteous goods at my gate.

units.zh: 所願者下不欺於地，中不欺於人，上不欺於天，以三不欺為素。
units.en: My wish is never to deceive earth below, men in the middle, or Heaven above—I make these three honesties my standard.
units.literal: What I desire is not to deceive below toward earth, not to deceive in the middle toward men, and not to deceive above toward Heaven—I take these three non-deceptions as my constant.

units.zh: 賤如是，貴如是，長如是，老如是，事親、事君、事長、臨人之道，曠蒙天恕，累經難而獲多福，曾陷蕃而歸中華，非人之謀，是天之祐。
units.en: Humble or exalted, young or old, I have been the same in serving parents, ruler, elders, and those I meet. Heaven has pardoned me; through repeated trials I have gained blessing; once captive among barbarians I returned to China—not by human design but by Heaven's grace.
units.literal: Lowly thus, noble thus, in youth thus, in age thus—in the ways of serving parents, serving the ruler, serving elders, and facing men. Broadly I have received Heaven's pardon; repeatedly passing through hardship I have gained many blessings; once trapped among the barbarians I returned to China—not by men's planning but by Heaven's aid.

units.zh: 六合之內有幸者，百歲之後有歸所。
units.en: Among all under heaven, the fortunate have a place to return to after a hundred years.
units.literal: Among all within the six directions, the fortunate have a place to return to after a hundred years.

units.zh: 無以珠玉含，當以時服斂，以籧篨葬，及擇不食之地而葬焉，以不及於古人故。
units.en: Put no pearls in my mouth; bury me in seasonable clothes in a plain bamboo coffin on untilled ground—for I do not measure up to the ancients.
units.literal: Do not place pearls and jade in my mouth; clothe me in garments of the season; bury me in a bamboo coffin; and choose untilled ground for burial—because I do not measure up to the ancients.

units.zh: 祭以特羊，戒殺生也，當以不害命之物祭。
units.en: Sacrifice with a single ram; I forbid killing—use offerings that do not take life.
units.literal: Sacrifice with a single ram; I admonish against taking life—offer what does not harm living creatures.

units.zh: 無立神道碑，以三代墳前不獲立碑故。
units.en: Erect no spirit-way stele, because in the Three Dynasties none was set before the tomb.
units.literal: Do not erect a spirit-way stele, because in the Three Dynasties no stele was set before the tomb.

units.zh: 無請謚號，以無德故。
units.en: Request no posthumous title, for I have no virtue.
units.literal: Do not request a posthumous title, for I have no virtue.

units.zh: 又念自賓佐至王佐及領藩鎮時，或有微益於國之事節，皆形於公籍。
units.en: I also recall that from aide to chief counselor and military governor, any small service to the state is in the public record.
units.literal: I also recall that from the time I was a guest aide to when I was a king's aide and governed a military commission, any small matter that benefited the state is recorded in the public registers.

units.zh: 所著文章篇詠，因多事散失外，收拾得者，編於家集，其間見其志，知之者，罪之者，未知眾寡矣。
units.en: My essays and poems, apart from many lost in busy times, are gathered in a family collection. Whether those who know my intent or condemn me are many or few, I cannot tell.
units.literal: The essays and poems I wrote, apart from many lost in the press of affairs, those I could recover are gathered into a family collection. Whether those who see my intent and know me, or those who condemn me, are many or few, I do not know.

units.zh: 有莊、有宅、有群書，有三子可以襲其業。
units.en: I have land, a house, many books, and three sons to carry on my work.
units.literal: I have estates, a residence, many books, and three sons who can carry on my work.

units.zh: 於此日五盥，日三省，尚猶日知其所亡，月無忘其所能。
units.en: Each day I bathe five times and examine myself thrice; still each day I learn what I lack and each month I remember what I can do.
units.literal: On this day I bathe five times and thrice daily examine myself; still each day I learn what I have lost, and each month I do not forget what I can do.

units.zh: 為子、為弟、為人臣、為師長、為夫、為父，有子、有猶子、有孫，奉身即有餘矣。
units.en: As son, brother, subject, teacher, husband, and father—with sons, a nephew's son, and grandsons—in my person I already have more than enough.
units.literal: As son, younger brother, subject, teacher, husband, and father—with sons, with a nephew's son, with grandsons—in sustaining my person I already have more than enough.

units.zh: 為時乃不足，不足者何？
units.en: For the times I am not enough—what is lacking?
units.literal: For the age I am not enough—what is it that is not enough?

units.zh: 不能為大君致一統、定八方，誠有愧於歷職歷官，何以答乾坤之施。
units.en: I could not bring unity to my lord or pacify the realm—I am ashamed of every office I have held. How can I repay Heaven and Earth?
units.literal: I could not bring unity to the great ruler or settle the eight directions—truly I am ashamed before every office I have held. How can I answer the gift of Heaven and Earth?

units.zh: 時開一卷，時飲一杯，食味別聲、被色，老安於當代耶！
units.en: Now and then I read, now and then I drink; I taste, listen, and dress in color—growing old at ease in my own time!
units.literal: Now and then I open a scroll, now and then I drink a cup; I taste flavors, distinguish sounds, and clothe myself in colors—growing old at ease in this age!

units.zh: 老而自樂，何樂如之！
units.en: Old and content—what greater joy is there!
units.literal: Old and joyful in myself—what joy could surpass this!

units.zh: 時乾祐三年朱明月長樂老序云。
units.en: Thus ends the preface of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy, dated the Zhu-ming month of Qianyou 3.
units.literal: Thus ends the preface of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy, dated the bright moon of the third year of Qianyou.

units.zh: 及太祖平內難，議立徐州節度使劉赟為漢嗣，遣道與秘書監趙上交、樞密直學士王度等往迎之。
units.en: When Taizu pacified the internal crisis, the court resolved to make Liu Yun of Xuzhou heir to Han and sent Dao with Zhao Shangjiao, Wang Du, and others to welcome him.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified the internal crisis, the court deliberated installing Liu Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, as heir to Han, and sent Dao with Director of the Secretariat Zhao Shangjiao, Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Du, and others to welcome him.

units.zh: 道尋與赟自徐赴汴，行至宋州，會澶州軍變。
units.en: Dao soon accompanied Yun from Xuzhou toward Bian; at Songzhou the Danzhou army mutinied.
units.literal: Dao soon accompanied Yun from Xu to Bian; when they reached Song Prefecture, the army at Dan Prefecture mutinied.

units.zh: 樞密使王峻遣郭崇領兵至，屯於衙門外，時道與上交等宿於衙內。
units.en: Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with troops, who camped outside the gate while Dao and Shangjiao lodged inside.
units.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with troops; they encamped outside the headquarters gate, while Dao and Shangjiao lodged inside.

units.zh: 是日，赟率左右甲士闔門登樓，詰崇所自，崇言太祖已副推戴。
units.en: That day Yun shut the gate, mounted the tower with his guards, and demanded where Chong came from. Chong said Taizu had already been acclaimed.
units.literal: That day Yun led his armored guards, shut the gate, and mounted the tower to question where Chong had come from. Chong said the Founding Emperor had already been chosen by acclamation.

units.zh: 左右知其事變，以為道所賣，皆欲殺道等以自快。
units.en: His attendants, learning what had happened, thought Dao had betrayed them and all wanted to kill Dao and the others.
units.literal: His attendants, learning of the turn of events, thought Dao had betrayed them and all wished to kill Dao and the others to vent their rage.

units.zh: 趙上交與王度聞之，皆惶怖不知所為，惟道偃仰自適，略無懼色，尋亦獲免焉。
units.en: Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du were terrified; only Dao reclined at ease without a trace of fear, and soon all were spared.
units.literal: Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du, hearing of it, were both terrified and did not know what to do; only Dao reclined at ease without the least sign of fear, and soon they were all spared.

units.zh: 道微時嘗賦詩云：「終聞海嶽歸明主，未省乾坤陷吉人。」
units.en: In his humble days Dao wrote: "Seas and mountains will return to the enlightened lord; Heaven and Earth do not trap the fortunate."
units.literal: In his humble days Dao once composed a poem: "In the end I hear that seas and mountains return to the enlightened lord; I have never seen Heaven and Earth trap a man of fortune.

units.zh: 至是其言驗矣。
units.en: On this occasion his words proved true.
units.literal: On this occasion his words were fulfilled.

units.zh: 〈（《青箱雜記》載馮道詩全篇云：莫為危時便愴神，前程往往有期因，終聞海嶽歸明主，未省乾坤陷吉人。
units.en: (Green Box Miscellany gives the full poem: Do not grieve in perilous times; the future has its cause. Seas and mountains return to the enlightened lord; Heaven and Earth do not trap the fortunate.)
units.literal: (Green Box Miscellany records Feng Dao's complete poem: Do not let perilous times sadden your spirit; the future often has its appointed cause. In the end I hear that seas and mountains return to the enlightened lord; I have never seen Heaven and Earth trap a man of fortune.)

units.zh: 道德幾時曾去世，舟車何處不通津，但教方寸無諸惡，狼虎叢中也立身。）〉
units.en: When did virtue leave the world? Where do boats and carts not cross? Keep the heart free of evil, and you may stand firm even among wolves and tigers.)〉
units.literal: When did virtue ever leave the world? Where do boats and carts not find a ford? Only teach the inch-square of the heart to harbor no evil, and you may stand firm even in a pack of wolves and tigers.)〉

units.zh: 廣順初，復拜太師、中書令，太祖甚重之，每進對不以名呼。
units.en: Early in Guangshun he was again Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat. Taizu greatly valued him and never called him by name in audience.
units.literal: Early in Guangshun he was again appointed Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat. The Founding Emperor greatly valued him and never addressed him by personal name when he came to audience.

units.zh: 及太祖崩，世宗以道為山陵使。
units.en: When Taizu died, Shizong made Dao tomb commissioner.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor died, Emperor Shizong made Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb.

units.zh: 會河東劉崇入寇，世宗召大臣議欲親征，道諫止之，世宗因言：「唐初，天下草寇蜂起，並是太宗親平之。」
units.en: When Liu Chong of Hedong invaded, Shizong summoned ministers to discuss campaigning in person. Dao urged him not to. Shizong said, "Early in Tang bandits rose everywhere, and Taizong pacified them himself."
units.literal: When Liu Chong of Hedong invaded, Shizong summoned the chief ministers to discuss a personal campaign. Dao admonished him to stop. Shizong then said, "Early in Tang, bandits rose everywhere like bees, and Emperor Taizong personally pacified them all.

units.zh: 道奏曰：「陛下得如太宗否？」
units.en: Dao said, "Can Your Majesty equal Taizong?"
units.literal: Dao memorialized, "Can Your Majesty equal Taizong?"

units.zh: 世宗怒曰：「馮道何相少也！」
units.en: Shizong snapped, "How Feng Dao underestimates me!"
units.literal: Shizong said angrily, "How Feng Dao underestimates me!"

units.zh: 乃罷。
units.en: The discussion ended.
units.literal: The discussion then ended.

units.zh: 及世宗親征，不及扈從，留道奉太祖山陵。
units.en: When Shizong campaigned in person, Dao could not accompany him and was left to oversee Taizu's tomb.
units.literal: When Shizong campaigned in person, Dao could not accompany him and was left to oversee the Founding Emperor's tomb rites.

units.zh: 時道已抱疾。
units.en: By then Dao was already ill.
units.literal: By then Dao was already ill.

units.zh: 及山陵禮畢，奉神主歸舊宮，未及祔廟，一夕薨於其第，時顯德元年四月十七日也，享年七十有三。
units.en: When the tomb rites ended he escorted the spirit tablet to the old palace; before it could enter the ancestral temple he died one night at home—on the seventeenth day of the fourth month of Xiande 1, aged seventy-three.
units.literal: When the tomb rites were finished he escorted the spirit tablet back to the old palace; before it could be installed in the ancestral temple, he died one night at his residence—on the seventeenth day of the fourth month of the first year of Xiande, at the age of seventy-three.

units.zh: 世宗聞之，輟視朝三日，冊贈尚書令，追封瀛王，謚曰文懿。
units.en: Shizong suspended court for three days, posthumously made him Director of the Department of State Affairs, Prince of Ying, and gave him the posthumous title Wényì.
units.literal: When Shizong heard of it he suspended court audiences for three days, posthumously appointed him Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed him posthumously as Prince of Ying, and gave him the posthumous title Cultured and Virtuous.

units.zh: 道歷任四朝，三入中書，在相位二十餘年，以持重鎮俗為己任，未嘗以片簡擾於諸侯，平生甚廉儉。
units.en: Dao served four dynasties, entered the Secretariat three times, and was chief minister for more than twenty years. He steadied custom through weighty conduct, never troubled the regional lords with a note, and lived very frugally.
units.literal: Dao served four dynasties, entered the Secretariat three times, and held the chief ministership for more than twenty years. He took steadying the customs through weighty conduct as his charge, never troubling the regional lords with a single note, and was very frugal throughout his life.

units.zh: 逮至末年，閨庭之內，稍徇奢靡，其子吉，尤恣狂蕩，道不能制，識者以其不終令譽，鹹嘆惜之。
units.en: In his last years his household grew somewhat luxurious; his son Ji was especially dissolute, and Dao could not control him. Knowing men regretted that his fine reputation did not endure.
units.literal: By his last years within the household he indulged luxury somewhat; his son Ji was especially unrestrained and dissolute, and Dao could not restrain him. Those who knew him, because his fine reputation did not last to the end, all sighed in regret.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：馮道之鎮同州也，有酒務吏乞以家財修夫子廟，道以狀付判官參詳其事。
units.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Feng Dao governed Tongzhou, a wine-monopoly clerk asked to repair the Confucius temple with his family wealth. Dao referred the petition to his judge.)
units.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Feng Dao governed Tong Prefecture, a clerk of the wine monopoly asked to repair the Confucius temple with his family wealth. Dao handed the petition to the judge for deliberation.)

units.zh: 判官素滑稽，因以一絕書判後云：「荊棘森森繞杏壇，儒官高貴盡偷安，若教酒務修夫子，覺我慚惶也大難。」
units.en: The judge was witty and appended a quatrain: "Thorns grow thick around the apricot altar; Confucian officials all steal their ease. If the wine office repairs the Master, my shame would be hard to bear."
units.literal: The judge was by nature witty and therefore wrote a quatrain at the end of his decision: "Thorns grow thick around the apricot altar; noble Confucian officials all steal their ease. If the wine monopoly is made to repair the Master, I feel my shame and dread would be very hard indeed.

units.zh: 道覽之有愧色，因出俸重創之。
units.en: Dao read it with shame and paid from his salary to rebuild the temple properly.
units.literal: When Dao read it he showed shame and therefore paid from his salary to rebuild the temple on a grand scale.

units.zh: 馮瀛王道之在中書也，有舉子李導投贄所業，馮相見之，戲謂曰：「老夫名道，其來久矣，加以累居相府，秀才不可謂不知，然亦名導，於禮可乎？」
units.en: When Feng Dao was in the Secretariat, a candidate named Li Dao presented his work. Feng jested, "My name is Dao and has been for a long time; you cannot fail to know it, having come to the chief minister's office—yet you are also named Dao. Is that proper?"
units.literal: When the Prince of Yingzhou Feng Dao was in the Secretariat, an examination candidate named Li Dao presented his work. The chief minister saw him and jested, "This old man's name is Dao and has long been so; added to repeated tenure in the chief minister's office, the scholar cannot be said not to know it—yet you are also named Dao. Is that proper in ritual?

units.zh: 李抗聲對曰：「相公是無寸底道字，小子有寸底導字，何謂不可也！」
