units.en: Li answered boldly, "Your Excellency's Dao has no 'inch' at the bottom; mine has an 'inch' at the bottom—how can it be improper!"
units.literal: Li answered boldly, "Your Excellency's character Dao has no inch at the bottom; this student's character Dao has an inch at the bottom—how can it be improper!"

units.zh: 公笑曰：「老夫不惟名無寸，諸事亦無寸，吾子可謂知人矣。」
units.en: Feng laughed and said, "I have no inch not only in my name but in anything. You truly know men."
units.literal: The duke laughed and said, "This old man not only has no inch in his name—he has no inch in anything. You may be called one who knows men."

units.zh: 了無怒色。
units.en: He showed no anger at all.
units.literal: He showed not the least anger.

units.zh: 馮吉，瀛王道之子，能彈琵琶，以皮為弦，世宗嘗令彈於御前，深欣善之，因號其琵琶曰「繞殿雷」也。
units.en: Feng Ji, Dao's son, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong had him play before the throne and greatly admired it, naming his pipa "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."
units.literal: Feng Ji, son of the Prince of Ying Feng Dao, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once had him play before the throne and greatly admired it, therefore naming his pipa "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."

units.zh: 道以其惰業，每加譴責，而吉攻之愈精，道益怒，凡與客飲，必使庭立而彈之，曲罷或賜以束帛，命背負之，然後致謝。
units.en: Dao often rebuked him for this idle craft, but Ji practiced all the harder, which angered Dao more. Whenever he entertained guests he made Ji play in the courtyard; when the piece ended he might give silk and make Ji carry it on his back before thanking him.
units.literal: Because of his idle craft Dao often rebuked him, but Ji practiced all the more diligently, which made Dao angrier still. Whenever he drank with guests he made Ji stand in the courtyard to play; when the piece ended he might bestow a bundle of silk and order him to carry it on his back before thanking him.

units.zh: 道自以為戒勖極矣，吉未能悛改，既而益自若。
units.en: Dao thought he had disciplined him to the limit, but Ji did not reform and grew even more at ease.
units.literal: Dao thought his admonition and discipline had reached the utmost, but Ji did not reform and afterward grew even more at ease.

units.zh: 道度無可奈何，嘆曰：「百工之司藝而身賤，理使然也。
units.en: Dao saw there was nothing to be done and sighed, "Among the hundred crafts, mastery of an art still means low station—that is how things are.
units.literal: Dao saw there was nothing to be done and sighed, "Among the hundred crafts, those who master an art remain low in station—it is the way of principle.

units.zh: 此子不過太常少卿耳。」
units.en: This boy will rise no higher than Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices."
units.literal: This boy will rise no higher than Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 其後果終於此。）〉
units.en: In the end he finished his career at exactly that rank.)〉
units.literal: In the end he indeed finished his career at that rank.)〉

units.zh: 史臣曰：道之履行，郁有古人之風；
units.en: The historiographer says: In conduct and bearing, Dao had the air of the ancients;
units.literal: The historiographer says: In conduct and bearing, Dao richly possessed the air of the ancients;

units.zh: 道之宇量，深得大臣之禮。
units.en: in breadth of spirit he deeply understood a great minister's rites.
units.literal: in breadth of spirit he deeply grasped the rites of a great minister.

units.zh: 然而事四朝，相六帝，可得為忠乎！
units.en: Yet serving four dynasties and counseling six emperors—can this be called loyalty?
units.literal: Yet serving four dynasties and counseling six emperors—can this be called loyalty!

units.zh: 夫一女二夫，人之不幸，況於再三者哉！
units.en: One woman with two husbands is misfortune enough—how much more a third!
units.literal: For one woman to have two husbands is a person's misfortune—how much more when it happens a third time!

units.zh: 所以飾終之典，不得謚為文貞、文忠者，蓋謂此也。
units.en: Therefore he was not given the posthumous titles Wénzhēn or Wénzhōng in the rites of death—this is what is meant.
units.literal: Therefore in the rites honoring him at the end he was not given the posthumous titles Cultured and Upright or Cultured and Loyal—this is what is meant.
